objective: Identify drugs targeting genes/pathways that minimize doxorubicin cardiotoxicity while preserving anti-tumor efficacy in NF1
disease_context: Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1) - loss of function tumor suppressor with hyperactive RAS/MAPK signaling in tumors
filtering_rationale: Prioritized drugs that: (1) inhibit cardiotoxicity mediators (TOP2B, CBR1), (2) enhance antioxidant defenses (NRF2, SOD2, GSH), (3) exploit tumor-specific vulnerabilities (MEK hyperactivation in NF1), (4) modulate DNA damage responses differentially between heart and tumor
data_sources: Open Targets (MAP2K1/MEK target: CHEMBL3587, TOP2B target: CHEMBL3396)
Note: ChEMBL API experienced timeouts - some drugs listed from established drug-target relationships pending verification

therapeutic_strategies.mechanism: Selectively inhibit TOP2B in cardiomyocytes to prevent doxorubicin-induced DNA damage and apoptosis, while preserving TOP2A activity in tumor cells for anti-cancer efficacy
therapeutic_strategies.rationale: TOP2B is the primary mediator of doxorubicin cardiotoxicity. Isoform-selective inhibition could provide cardioprotection without compromising tumor response. Challenge: TOP2A and TOP2B share high sequence similarity.

drugs.name: Dexrazoxane
drugs.mechanism: Iron chelator that prevents formation of TOP2-DNA cleavage complexes; reduces doxorubicin cardiotoxicity via TOP2B pathway inhibition
drugs.selectivity: Non-selective TOP2 inhibitor - affects both TOP2A and TOP2B. May reduce tumor efficacy at high doses.
drugs.clinical_status: FDA approved for prevention of anthracycline cardiotoxicity in adults with metastatic breast cancer
drugs.nf1_relevance: Could be used prophylactically in NF1 patients requiring doxorubicin for MPNST or other tumors
drugs.evidence_level: HIGH - Multiple clinical trials demonstrate cardioprotection

excluded_candidates.name: Etoposide
excluded_candidates.reason: TOP2 poison that stabilizes TOP2-DNA complexes (opposite mechanism needed); would increase cardiotoxicity

excluded_candidates.name: Mitoxantrone
excluded_candidates.reason: TOP2 poison with known cardiotoxicity; contraindicated for cardioprotection strategy

therapeutic_strategies.mechanism: Block carbonyl reductase 1 to prevent conversion of doxorubicin to the more cardiotoxic metabolite doxorubicinol
therapeutic_strategies.rationale: CBR1 inhibition shown to reduce doxorubicinol formation in preclinical models. No FDA-approved selective CBR1 inhibitors currently available.

drugs.name: Quercetin
drugs.mechanism: Flavonoid with weak CBR1 inhibitory activity; also has antioxidant properties
drugs.phase: Dietary supplement (not FDA approved as drug)
drugs.selectivity: Non-selective; inhibits multiple reductases and has broad polyphenol activities
drugs.clinical_status: Available as nutritional supplement; limited clinical trial data for cardioprotection
drugs.nf1_relevance: Low risk adjunct therapy but limited potency for CBR1 inhibition
drugs.evidence_level: LOW - Preclinical data only for CBR1 inhibition

excluded_candidates.name: Specific CBR1 inhibitors
excluded_candidates.reason: No FDA-approved or clinically advanced selective CBR1 inhibitors identified. This remains a drug development opportunity.

therapeutic_strategies.mechanism: Activate NRF2 transcription factor to upregulate antioxidant genes (SOD2, CAT, GPX1, GSTs) that protect against doxorubicin-induced oxidative stress
therapeutic_strategies.rationale: NRF2 is master regulator of antioxidant response. Multiple drugs target this pathway. Activation protects heart without interfering with tumor TOP2 targeting.

drugs.name: Bardoxolone methyl
drugs.mechanism: Potent NRF2 activator via KEAP1 inhibition; induces antioxidant response element (ARE)-driven gene expression including SOD2, CAT, GPX1, GSTM1, GSTP1
drugs.phase: Phase 3 (clinical trials for chronic kidney disease)
drugs.clinical_status: Investigational - Phase 3 trials ongoing; previously tested in diabetic nephropathy (trials terminated due to cardiovascular events, but different patient population)
drugs.nf1_relevance: Could provide broad cardioprotection via antioxidant upregulation in NF1 patients receiving doxorubicin
drugs.evidence_level: MODERATE - Phase 3 data available but safety concerns in some populations

drugs.name: Sulforaphane
drugs.mechanism: Natural isothiocyanate from broccoli; NRF2 activator via KEAP1 cysteine modification
drugs.phase: Dietary supplement / nutraceutical (Phase 2 trials for various indications)
drugs.selectivity: NRF2 pathway activator with additional histone deacetylase inhibitory activity
drugs.clinical_status: Available as supplement; limited Phase 2 trial data for cancer prevention
drugs.nf1_relevance: Low-risk adjunct with antioxidant and potential anti-cancer properties
drugs.evidence_level: LOW-MODERATE - Preclinical cardioprotection data; limited clinical validation

drugs.name: Dimethyl fumarate (DMF)
drugs.mechanism: NRF2 activator; FDA-approved for multiple sclerosis
drugs.clinical_status: FDA approved for relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (brand name: Tecfidera)
drugs.nf1_relevance: Repurposing opportunity for cardioprotection; established safety profile
drugs.evidence_level: MODERATE - FDA approved but not tested specifically for doxorubicin cardioprotection

therapeutic_strategies.mechanism: Superoxide dismutase mimetics scavenge reactive oxygen species generated by doxorubicin metabolism
therapeutic_strategies.rationale: Direct ROS scavenging complements NRF2 activation. SOD2 upregulation is cardioprotective endpoint of NRF2 pathway.

drugs.name: Avasopasem manganese (GC4419)
drugs.mechanism: Selective SOD mimetic; dismutates superoxide to hydrogen peroxide, reducing oxidative damage
drugs.clinical_status: Investigational - Phase 3 trials for cancer treatment-related toxicities
drugs.nf1_relevance: Could reduce doxorubicin-induced ROS in cardiac tissue
drugs.evidence_level: MODERATE - Phase 3 data for radiation toxicity; preclinical data for anthracycline cardioprotection

drugs.name: MnTBAP (Mn(III)tetrakis(4-benzoic acid)porphyrin)
drugs.mechanism: Manganese porphyrin SOD mimetic and peroxynitrite scavenger
drugs.clinical_status: Research compound - not in clinical development
drugs.nf1_relevance: Preclinical proof-of-concept for cardioprotection but no clinical pathway

therapeutic_strategies.mechanism: Exploit hyperactive RAS/MAPK signaling in NF1-deficient tumors. MEK inhibition reduces TOP2A expression selectively in RAS-driven tumors, reducing their doxorubicin sensitivity. PARADOX: This could reduce tumor efficacy, OR could be used to dose-reduce doxorubicin if MEK inhibitor has direct anti-tumor activity in NF1 tumors.
therapeutic_strategies.rationale: MEK inhibitors are FDA-approved for NF1-related tumors (plexiform neurofibromas). Could be combined with reduced-dose doxorubicin to maintain efficacy while reducing cardiotoxicity.

drugs.name: Selumetinib (AZD6244)
drugs.mechanism: Selective allosteric MEK1/2 inhibitor; blocks ERK phosphorylation downstream of RAS
drugs.clinical_status: FDA approved for NF1-associated inoperable plexiform neurofibromas in pediatric patients (brand name: Koselugo)
drugs.nf1_relevance: CRITICAL - Already approved for NF1 tumors. Could be combined with doxorubicin in NF1-associated MPNST or other tumors requiring anthracyclines.
drugs.evidence_level: HIGH - FDA approved specifically for NF1

drugs.name: Trametinib (GSK1120212)
drugs.mechanism: Selective allosteric MEK1/2 inhibitor
drugs.clinical_status: FDA approved for BRAF V600-mutant melanoma and NSCLC
drugs.nf1_relevance: Could be repurposed for NF1 tumors; more potent than selumetinib but not specifically approved for NF1
drugs.evidence_level: HIGH - FDA approved for RAS pathway-driven cancers

drugs.name: Cobimetinib (GDC-0973)
drugs.mechanism: Selective allosteric MEK1/2 inhibitor
drugs.clinical_status: FDA approved for BRAF V600-mutant melanoma in combination with vemurafenib
drugs.nf1_relevance: Could be repurposed for NF1 tumors
drugs.evidence_level: HIGH - FDA approved for RAS pathway-driven cancers

excluded_candidates.name: MEK activators
excluded_candidates.reason: No MEK activators clinically available; would be contraindicated in NF1 (already hyperactive pathway)

therapeutic_strategies.mechanism: PARP inhibitors block DNA repair in tumor cells (synthetic lethality with doxorubicin-induced damage), but may also protect cardiomyocytes by preventing PARP1-mediated energy depletion and cell death. BIDIRECTIONAL EFFECT - needs careful evaluation.
therapeutic_strategies.rationale: PARP inhibitors are FDA-approved and could synergize with doxorubicin in tumors. However, PARP1 interacts with TOP2B (Phase 3 data) and PARP inhibition might increase cardiotoxicity. Preclinical validation needed.

drugs.name: Olaparib (AZD2281)
drugs.mechanism: PARP1/2 inhibitor; traps PARP on DNA causing synthetic lethality in BRCA-deficient or HR-deficient tumors
drugs.clinical_status: FDA approved for BRCA-mutant ovarian, breast, pancreatic, and prostate cancers
drugs.nf1_relevance: Could synergize with doxorubicin in NF1 tumors IF they have HR deficiency. Risk of increased cardiotoxicity needs evaluation.
drugs.evidence_level: MODERATE - FDA approved for cancer but cardiotoxicity interaction with doxorubicin uncertain
drugs.caution: PARP1-TOP2B interaction (BioGRID) suggests potential for increased cardiotoxicity; requires preclinical validation

drugs.name: Rucaparib (AG-014699)
drugs.mechanism: PARP1/2/3 inhibitor
drugs.clinical_status: FDA approved for BRCA-mutant ovarian and prostate cancers
drugs.nf1_relevance: Similar to olaparib - potential synergy but cardiotoxicity risk

drugs.name: Niraparib
drugs.mechanism: PARP1/2 inhibitor
drugs.clinical_status: FDA approved for ovarian, fallopian tube, and peritoneal cancers
drugs.nf1_relevance: Similar profile to other PARP inhibitors

drugs.name: Talazoparib
drugs.mechanism: Ultra-potent PARP1/2 inhibitor with strong PARP-trapping activity
drugs.selectivity: Highly selective for PARP1/2; strongest trapping activity
drugs.clinical_status: FDA approved for BRCA-mutant breast cancer
drugs.nf1_relevance: Most potent PARP inhibitor - highest synergy potential but also highest cardiotoxicity risk
drugs.caution: Strongest PARP trapping may increase cardiotoxicity

excluded_candidates.name: PARP activators
excluded_candidates.reason: No PARP activators in clinical development; would increase DNA repair in tumors (counterproductive)

therapeutic_strategies.mechanism: HDAC inhibitors modulate chromatin structure and can suppress TOP2B expression in cardiac tissue while maintaining TOP2A in proliferating tumor cells. Also shown to affect doxorubicin sensitivity.
therapeutic_strategies.rationale: HDAC1/2 interact with TOP2B (Phase 3 BioGRID data). Multiple FDA-approved HDAC inhibitors available. Tissue-selective effects possible due to differential proliferation rates.

drugs.name: Vorinostat (SAHA)
drugs.mechanism: Pan-HDAC inhibitor (Class I, II, IV); induces histone hyperacetylation and altered gene expression
drugs.clinical_status: FDA approved for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
drugs.nf1_relevance: Could modulate TOP2B expression in cardiac tissue; may sensitize or protect depending on context
drugs.evidence_level: MODERATE - FDA approved but mechanism in cardioprotection needs validation
drugs.caution: HDAC inhibitors can both sensitize and protect - bidirectional effects require careful dosing

drugs.name: Romidepsin (FK228)
drugs.mechanism: Selective HDAC1/2 inhibitor (Class I)
drugs.clinical_status: FDA approved for cutaneous and peripheral T-cell lymphoma
drugs.nf1_relevance: More selective than vorinostat for HDAC1/2-TOP2B interaction

drugs.name: Belinostat (PXD101)
drugs.mechanism: Pan-HDAC inhibitor
drugs.clinical_status: FDA approved for peripheral T-cell lymphoma
drugs.nf1_relevance: Similar profile to vorinostat

drugs.name: Panobinostat (LBH589)
drugs.mechanism: Pan-HDAC inhibitor
drugs.clinical_status: FDA approved for multiple myeloma
drugs.nf1_relevance: Most potent HDAC inhibitor; highest risk of off-target effects
drugs.caution: Known cardiac adverse effects in some patients - careful monitoring required

therapeutic_strategies.mechanism: Support glutathione-dependent detoxification of doxorubicin and ROS. Enhance GST and GPX1 function.
therapeutic_strategies.rationale: GSTM1 and GSTP1 are protective (Phase 2 data). Glutathione supplementation is safe and well-tolerated. NAC is FDA-approved for acetaminophen overdose.

drugs.name: N-acetylcysteine (NAC)
drugs.mechanism: Glutathione precursor; provides cysteine for glutathione synthesis; direct antioxidant via free thiol group
drugs.selectivity: Non-selective antioxidant; supports multiple glutathione-dependent pathways
drugs.clinical_status: FDA approved for acetaminophen overdose; used off-label for antioxidant support
drugs.nf1_relevance: Safe, well-tolerated adjunct for glutathione support in NF1 patients receiving doxorubicin
drugs.evidence_level: MODERATE - FDA approved but limited data specifically for doxorubicin cardioprotection in humans

drugs.name: Glutathione (GSH)
drugs.mechanism: Direct glutathione supplementation; substrate for GSTs and GPX
drugs.clinical_status: Available as supplement and IV preparation; limited clinical trial data
drugs.nf1_relevance: Oral bioavailability limited; IV administration may be more effective
drugs.evidence_level: LOW - Preclinical data; oral GSH has poor bioavailability

excluded_candidates.name: Buthionine sulfoximine (BSO)
excluded_candidates.reason: Glutathione synthesis inhibitor - would INCREASE doxorubicin toxicity; used to sensitize tumors but contraindicated for cardioprotection

therapeutic_strategies.mechanism: Estrogen receptor activation provides cardioprotection via multiple pathways including antioxidant gene expression. Female sex and estrogen status correlate with reduced doxorubicin cardiotoxicity.
therapeutic_strategies.rationale: ESR1 identified as moderate priority target. Selective estrogen receptor modulators (SERMs) could provide cardioprotection in appropriate patient populations.

drugs.name: Tamoxifen
drugs.mechanism: Selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM); agonist in some tissues (bone, cardiovascular), antagonist in breast
drugs.clinical_status: FDA approved for breast cancer prevention and treatment
drugs.nf1_relevance: Could provide cardioprotection via ESR1 activation in heart; may be useful in female NF1 patients with ER+ breast tumors requiring doxorubicin
drugs.evidence_level: LOW-MODERATE - FDA approved but cardioprotection mechanism not well-studied

drugs.name: Raloxifene
drugs.mechanism: SERM with cardiovascular agonist activity
drugs.clinical_status: FDA approved for osteoporosis prevention and breast cancer risk reduction
drugs.nf1_relevance: Potentially safer SERM profile than tamoxifen for cardioprotection

excluded_candidates.name: Aromatase inhibitors
excluded_candidates.reason: Would reduce estrogen levels and potentially increase cardiotoxicity risk

drugs.name: Dexrazoxane
drugs.mechanism: Iron chelator; TOP2B pathway inhibitor preventing doxorubicin-DNA-TOP2B complex formation
drugs.rationale: PRIMARY CARDIOPROTECTIVE AGENT - FDA approved specifically for preventing anthracycline cardiotoxicity. Strong clinical evidence but may reduce tumor efficacy at high doses.
drugs.nf1_specific: Standard of care option for NF1 patients at high risk for cardiotoxicity

drugs.name: Selumetinib
drugs.mechanism: Selective MEK1/2 inhibitor; blocks hyperactive RAS/MAPK pathway in NF1 tumors
drugs.phase: FDA Approved (Phase 4) for NF1 plexiform neurofibromas
drugs.rationale: FDA-APPROVED FOR NF1 - Could enable doxorubicin dose reduction or be combined at lower doses. Exploits NF1-specific tumor vulnerability.
drugs.nf1_specific: CRITICAL - Already approved for NF1; established safety profile in NF1 patients

drugs.name: Bardoxolone methyl
drugs.mechanism: Potent NRF2 activator; upregulates SOD2, CAT, GPX1, GSTs for comprehensive antioxidant protection
drugs.rationale: Master antioxidant regulator - addresses multiple cardiotoxicity mechanisms (ROS, oxidative stress, mitochondrial damage). Phase 3 data available.
drugs.nf1_specific: Not NF1-specific but targets fundamental cardiotoxicity mechanisms
drugs.caution: Previous trial terminations due to cardiovascular events in diabetic nephropathy patients

drugs.name: Trametinib
drugs.mechanism: Selective MEK1/2 inhibitor; most potent approved MEK inhibitor
drugs.rationale: More potent than selumetinib; could be repurposed for NF1 tumors requiring doxorubicin
drugs.nf1_specific: Not approved for NF1 but targets same pathway as selumetinib

drugs.name: Cobimetinib
drugs.mechanism: Selective MEK1/2 inhibitor
drugs.rationale: Alternative MEK inhibitor with established safety profile

drugs.name: Olaparib
drugs.mechanism: PARP1/2 inhibitor with DNA repair blocking and PARP-trapping activity
drugs.rationale: Could synergize with doxorubicin in tumors but PARP1-TOP2B interaction raises cardiotoxicity concerns. Requires preclinical validation.
drugs.nf1_specific: Not NF1-specific; applicability depends on HR deficiency status of tumor
drugs.caution: PARP1-TOP2B protein interaction (BioGRID) suggests potential for increased cardiotoxicity

drugs.name: Avasopasem manganese (GC4419)
drugs.mechanism: Selective SOD mimetic; dismutates superoxide radicals
drugs.rationale: Direct ROS scavenging; Phase 3 data for cancer treatment toxicity reduction

drugs.name: N-acetylcysteine (NAC)
drugs.mechanism: Glutathione precursor; supports GST-mediated detoxification and GPX antioxidant function
drugs.rationale: Safe, well-tolerated adjunct; supports protective enzymes identified in Phase 2

drugs.name: Dimethyl fumarate
drugs.mechanism: NRF2 activator; FDA-approved for multiple sclerosis
drugs.rationale: Repurposing opportunity; established safety profile for chronic use

drugs.name: Vorinostat
drugs.mechanism: Pan-HDAC inhibitor; modulates TOP2B expression via chromatin remodeling
drugs.rationale: HDAC1/2 interact with TOP2B (BioGRID data from Phase 3); could suppress cardiac TOP2B expression
drugs.caution: Bidirectional effects on drug sensitivity require careful evaluation

drugs.name: Romidepsin
drugs.mechanism: Class I-selective HDAC inhibitor
drugs.rationale: More selective than vorinostat for HDAC1/2-TOP2B pathway

drugs.name: Sulforaphane
drugs.mechanism: Natural NRF2 activator from broccoli
drugs.selectivity: NRF2 activation with HDAC inhibitory activity
drugs.rationale: Safe, accessible adjunct with antioxidant and potential anti-cancer properties

excluded_candidates.name: Etoposide
excluded_candidates.reason: TOP2 poison - stabilizes TOP2-DNA complexes (opposite of needed mechanism); would increase cardiotoxicity
excluded_candidates.mechanism_conflict: Requires TOP2 poisoning for anti-tumor activity; incompatible with cardioprotection strategy

excluded_candidates.name: Mitoxantrone
excluded_candidates.reason: Anthracenedione with known cardiotoxicity via TOP2B pathway; contraindicated for cardioprotection

excluded_candidates.name: Buthionine sulfoximine (BSO)
excluded_candidates.reason: Glutathione synthesis inhibitor - would INCREASE doxorubicin toxicity; used in research to sensitize tumors but contraindicated clinically

excluded_candidates.name: Aromatase inhibitors (letrozole, anastrozole, exemestane)
excluded_candidates.reason: Reduce estrogen levels; would eliminate potential cardioprotective effects of estrogen signaling

excluded_candidates.name: Non-selective CBR1 inhibitors
excluded_candidates.reason: No FDA-approved selective CBR1 inhibitors available; quercetin has weak activity but limited clinical utility
excluded_candidates.mechanism_conflict: Drug development gap - target validated but no clinical compounds

nf1_specific_combinations.rationale: NF1-associated tumors (plexiform neurofibromas, MPNST, gliomas) may require anthracycline-based chemotherapy. Combining cardioprotective and NF1-targeted therapies could improve outcomes.

proposed_combinations.mechanism: Anti-tumor (doxorubicin TOP2A targeting) + NF1 pathway inhibition (selumetinib MEK) + cardioprotection (dexrazoxane TOP2B blocking)
proposed_combinations.rationale: Selumetinib FDA-approved for NF1; dexrazoxane FDA-approved for cardioprotection; both have established safety profiles
proposed_combinations.clinical_precedent: Selumetinib approved as monotherapy for NF1 plexiform neurofibromas; combination with doxorubicin not yet tested

proposed_combinations.rationale: Comprehensive antioxidant strategy targeting multiple protective pathways
proposed_combinations.clinical_precedent: No direct precedent but both compounds have been tested in clinical trials
proposed_combinations.caution: Bardoxolone has previous cardiovascular safety signals

proposed_combinations.mechanism: MEK inhibition provides anti-tumor activity in NF1 tumors, allowing doxorubicin dose reduction
proposed_combinations.rationale: Dose reduction is most effective cardioprotection strategy; selumetinib could maintain efficacy at lower doxorubicin doses
proposed_combinations.clinical_precedent: Selumetinib monotherapy effective for NF1 plexiform neurofibromas

proposed_combinations.mechanism: HDAC inhibition may suppress cardiac TOP2B expression while dexrazoxane blocks remaining TOP2B activity
proposed_combinations.rationale: Dual TOP2B targeting via transcriptional suppression and enzymatic inhibition
proposed_combinations.clinical_precedent: HDAC inhibitors combined with other chemotherapies in clinical trials
proposed_combinations.caution: HDAC inhibitors can have bidirectional effects on drug sensitivity

existing_clinical_trials.note: No clinical trials identified combining doxorubicin with selumetinib in NF1 patients. This represents a significant opportunity given selumetinib's FDA approval for NF1.
existing_clinical_trials.search_needed: ClinicalTrials.gov search for 'doxorubicin AND selumetinib AND NF1' or 'anthracycline AND MEK inhibitor AND neurofibromatosis'

immediate_clinical_use: Dexrazoxane - FDA approved for anthracycline cardioprotection
Selumetinib - FDA approved for NF1 plexiform neurofibromas
NAC - FDA approved, safe adjunct for antioxidant support
clinical_development_ready: Trametinib/Cobimetinib - FDA approved MEK inhibitors (repurposing for NF1)
requires_preclinical_validation: PARP inhibitors (olaparib, rucaparib, niraparib, talazoparib) - cardiotoxicity interaction uncertain
HDAC inhibitors (vorinostat, romidepsin) - bidirectional effects need clarification
TOP2B-selective inhibitors - none currently available (drug development opportunity)
drug_development_gaps: Selective CBR1 inhibitors - target validated but no clinical compounds
TOP2B-selective inhibitors - isoform selectivity remains major challenge
Tissue-selective NRF2 activators - cardiac-specific targeting would be ideal

highest_priority_drugs.rationale: FDA-approved for NF1; directly addresses tumor biology; could enable doxorubicin dose reduction
highest_priority_drugs.evidence: Phase 3 NF1 trial data (NCT01362803); FDA approval 2020

highest_priority_drugs.rationale: FDA-approved specifically for anthracycline cardioprotection; direct TOP2B mechanism
highest_priority_drugs.evidence: Multiple RCTs showing cardioprotection; FDA approved

highest_priority_drugs.rationale: Potent NRF2 activator targeting master antioxidant regulator; Phase 3 development
highest_priority_drugs.evidence: Phase 3 trials in CKD; preclinical cardioprotection data

novel_insights: Selumetinib (NF1-approved MEK inhibitor) represents unique opportunity to address both tumor biology AND enable cardioprotection via doxorubicin dose reduction
NRF2 pathway activation (bardoxolone, DMF, sulforaphane) provides comprehensive antioxidant response addressing multiple cardiotoxicity mechanisms
PARP1-TOP2B protein interaction (BioGRID data from Phase 3) suggests PARP inhibitors may INCREASE cardiotoxicity despite potential tumor synergy - requires careful evaluation
HDAC1/2-TOP2B interactions suggest epigenetic modulation as alternative cardioprotection strategy
Major drug development gap: No selective CBR1 inhibitors or TOP2B-selective inhibitors currently available despite strong target validation
nf1_specific_opportunities: Selumetinib + doxorubicin combination could be NF1 disease-modifying while enabling safer chemotherapy
MEK pathway hyperactivation in NF1 tumors creates synthetic lethality opportunity with lower doxorubicin doses
NF1 patients may benefit from prophylactic cardioprotection given potential need for repeated chemotherapy cycles

limitations_and_caveats.api_limitations: ChEMBL API experienced timeouts during searches. Some ChEMBL IDs marked 'requires verification' are based on established drug-target relationships but not confirmed via API during this session.
evidence_gaps: Limited clinical trial data for most cardioprotection strategies beyond dexrazoxane
No clinical trials combining selumetinib with doxorubicin in NF1
PARP inhibitor cardiotoxicity interaction with doxorubicin poorly characterized
Optimal timing and dosing of cardioprotective agents relative to doxorubicin administration not established for most candidates
mechanistic_uncertainties: PARP inhibitors: Could be tumor-synergistic OR cardiotoxic - bidirectional possibility
HDAC inhibitors: Can both sensitize and protect depending on dose, timing, and specific isoform
MEK inhibitors: Reduce TOP2A in tumors which could reduce doxorubicin efficacy OR create synthetic lethality
NRF2 activators: Could theoretically protect tumor cells as well as cardiomyocytes - differential effects need validation
limitations_and_caveats.recommendation: Prioritize drugs with clinical precedent (dexrazoxane, selumetinib, NAC) while pursuing preclinical validation of mechanistically rational but clinically unproven combinations (bardoxolone, HDAC inhibitors, PARP inhibitors with careful cardiotoxicity monitoring)
